title: Anharmonicity and Nonadiabaticity in Hydride Superconductors
authors: Shashi B. Mishra, Francesco Belli, Eva Zurek, Elena R. Margine
abstract: We study superconductivity in representative hydrides using anharmonic phonons, electron-phonon vertex corrections, and full-bandwidth Eliashberg theory. The high-pressure binary hydrides H3S, YH6, and YH9 must be treated with both anharmonic and nonadiabatic corrections, whereas the ambient-pressure PdH/PdD/PdT series is strongly anharmonic but remains adiabatic, reproducing the inverse isotope effect without sizable vertex contributions. LaBeH8 exhibits weak anharmonicity, while vertex corrections reduce the critical temperature (Tc) by approximately 4 K, leaving the predicted Tc above experiment. To identify when treatments beyond harmonic, adiabatic Migdal-Eliashberg theory are required, we introduce the anharmonic renormalization $A_λ$ and the vertex ratio $R_{V}$ as material-specific diagnostics.
summary: This paper investigates superconducting properties in hydrides by incorporating anharmonic phonon effects and nonadiabatic vertex corrections into Eliashberg theory. The authors introduce diagnostics, such as the anharmonic renormalization factor $A_\lambda$ and vertex ratio $R_V$, to guide researchers on when simple theoretical models break down. By applying these advanced methods, they achieve better agreement with experimental critical temperatures for several high-pressure superconductors.
main_problem: The study aims to determine when advanced theoretical treatments beyond standard harmonic, adiabatic Migdal-Eliashberg theory are necessary for accurately describing superconductivity in various hydride materials.
main_result: The authors successfully applied anharmonic and nonadiabatic corrections to predict superconducting critical temperatures ($T_c$) for several hydrides, showing that these effects are crucial for matching experimental values.
method: They employed full-bandwidth Eliashberg theory combined with density-functional theory (DFT) calculations incorporating anharmonic phonon renormalization and electron-phonon vertex corrections.
model_or_system: The research focuses on superconductivity in high-pressure binary hydrides ($	ext{H}_3	ext{S}$, $	ext{YH}_6$, $	ext{YH}_9$) and ambient-pressure Pd hydride series, using advanced phonon calculations (ML/SSCHA).
key_observables: Critical Temperature ($T_c$), electron-phonon coupling constants ($\lambda_{	ext{anh}}$, $\lambda_{	ext{har}}$), anharmonic renormalization diagnostic ($A_\lambda$), and vertex ratio ($R_V$).
important_parameters: The adiabaticity ratio ($\eta$) is key for distinguishing between regimes, with small values suggesting the breakdown of Migdal's approximation.
main_assumptions: The central theme involves testing the limits of approximations: moving beyond harmonic lattice dynamics (anharmonicity) and accounting for vertex corrections (nonadiabaticity).
figures_summary: Figures compare calculated $T_c$ values across different theoretical treatments (harmonic vs. anharmonic + vertex) against experimental data for various hydrides.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes several material classes, introducing diagnostics ($A_\lambda$, $R_V$) to classify the required level of theory—from simple harmonic models up to full nonadiabatic corrections.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter superconductivity, the rigorous development and application of advanced many-body perturbation theory (Eliashberg formalism) and the introduction of material-specific diagnostic criteria ($A_\lambda$, $R_V$) for theoretical model selection are highly relevant to open quantum systems.
